definitions.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part 1
definitions.statement: If f is continuous on [a, b], then the accumulation function F(x) = int_a^x f(t) dt is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), and its derivative is exactly f(x).
conditions: f must be continuous on [a, b]
definitions.explanation: FTC Part 1 establishes that differentiation and integration are inverse mathematical operations.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Every continuous function possesses an antiderivative defined by its accumulation integral.

definitions.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part 2 (Evaluation Theorem)
definitions.latex: \int_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), \quad \text{where } F'(x) = f(x)
definitions.statement: If f is continuous on [a, b] and F is any antiderivative of f, then the definite integral equals the net change of F across the interval.
definitions.explanation: Replaces exhaustive limits of Riemann sums with simple algebraic evaluation of antiderivatives at endpoints.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Definite integrals equal the difference in values of any antiderivative at interval endpoints.
